dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: varṇasya savisargasya visargāntaṃ citiṃ kuru | nirādhāreṇa cittena spṛśed brahma sanātanam ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: Place awareness at the end of the visarga of a syllable that carries a visarga (the out-breathed 'ḥ'); with a mind free of support, one touches the eternal brahman.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: Abhinavagupta (Tantrāloka 3.143) and a verse quoted by Śivopādhyāya identify visarga with the creative power (kaulikī śakti) from which the cosmos emanates; written as two dots after a letter, it is spoken as a soft 'ḥ'. Fixing the mind at the very end of that sound, the symbol of manifestation, the mind is detached from manifestation and slips into the void, steeped in the silence of brahman.
dharana.technique_name: At the End of the Out-Breathed 'Ḥ'
dharana.instruction: Softly sound 'aḥ' and rest attention at the exact point where the breathy 'ḥ' fades into silence.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 91 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: its very end, where it becomes silence
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is a syllable ending in a soft breath-sound, and the exact point where that breath-sound becomes silence.
geometry.svg_hint: a short line ending in a feathered trail that fades into an open dot
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Follow the 'ḥ' out
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: attention rides a soft breath-sound to its end and is left without support, in silence. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: the silence at the end of the soft 'ḥ'
breath.cue: Natural in-breath. On the out-breath, sound 'aḥ' softly and let the 'ḥ' trail away with the breath. A free breath between rounds. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Follow the sound to its very end
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The very end of the soft out-breathed 'ḥ'

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Place awareness at the end of the visarga of a syllable that carries a visarga (the out-breathed 'ḥ'); with a mind free of support, one touches the eternal brahman.
adiyogi.method_summary: Sound 'aḥ' softly on an out-breath, so that it ends in a gentle breathy 'ḥ'. Place awareness at the exact point where the 'ḥ' fades into silence, and rest there with the mind leaning on nothing.

honesty.disclosure: Door 068 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 68 (verse 91) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Keep the out-breath soft and unforced; take free breaths between rounds. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
